"The Matanga Jataka tells the story of the Bodhisatta who was born as a Chandala named Matanga. Once, he went into the city of Varanasi on some business, where he encountered Dittha Mangalika, the daughter of a wealthy merchant. On seeing him, she washed her eyes, exclaiming, 'I have seen something inauspicious!' Her angry attendants beat up Matanga. In protest, Matanga lay down at the door of her father's house, refusing to eat for seven days. Ultimately, the merchant gave him Dittha Mangalika in marriage. questionText:
Read the following excerpt carefully and answer the question that follows:

"Draupadi is supposed to have asked Yudhishthira whether he had lost himself before staking her in the fateful game of dice. Two contrary opinions were expressed in response. One was that even if Yudhishthira had lost himself earlier, his wife remained under his control, so he could stake her. The other was that an unfree man (as Yudhishthira had become when he lost himself) could not stake another person, especially a free human being. The matter remained unresolved; ultimately Dhritarashtra restored to the Pandavas and Draupadi their personal freedom. "The Matanga Jataka tells the story of the Bodhisatta who was born as a Chandala named Matanga. Once, he went into the city of Varanasi on some business, where he encountered Dittha Mangalika, the daughter of a wealthy merchant. On seeing him, she washed her eyes, exclaiming, 'I have seen something inauspicious!' Her angry attendants beat up Matanga. In protest, Matanga lay down at the door of her father's house, refusing to eat for seven days. Ultimately, the merchant gave him Dittha Mangalika in marriage. Later, Matanga renounced the world and attained immense spiritual powers, showing that virtue and spiritual wisdom transcend caste boundaries."

In Buddhist tradition, who was the Bodhisatta depicted in this Jataka tale?
